newsitem.title: USA: U.S. envoy rejects N. Korea linkage on peace talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy rejects N. Korea linkage on peace talks.

text.p: The U.S. ambassador to the United Nations rejected on Friday a North Korean demand for more food aid as a condition for taking part in four-party peace talks aimed at formally ending the Korean War.

"We explicitly reject the linkage," Ambassador Bill Richardson said in a telephone interview. But he predicted the world community might respond more positively to North Korea's needs if it joined the talks.
"If North Korea accepts the four-party talks the international community, in my judgment, might respond more positively to North Korea's humanitarian needs in the future," he said.

The South Korean Foreign Ministry in Seoul said North Korea conditionally offered to join the talks at a meeting in New York on Wednesday of working-level officials from the two Koreas and the United States. The fourth party to the talks would be China.
At issue is replacing the armistice of 1953 that ended the fighting on the Korean peninsula with a formal peace agreement.
Vice President Al Gore arrived in Seoul on Friday after a five-day visit to China during which he discussed the four-party talks.

"We've told them (North Korea) there will be a great deal of goodwill ... if you come into this four-party process. If you come into them, good things will happen," an official travelling with Gore told reporters.
